title: A full mixture test adds six failures at a 0.10 change limit in 607 selected Allen recovery curves
abstract: We tested whether a full same-sign positive exponential-mixture rule adds exclusions after four-point sign and divided-difference checks. Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 supplied 607 selected mouse VisP and human TCx connections with at least five trials at each of four pauses. We mapped the model to a cone generated by (1,x,x^3,x^15) for x in [0,1]. Adaptive linear programs and global polynomial bounds gave lower and upper uniform-distance bounds. At an assumed change limit of 0.10 normalized units, 483 curves failed the full test. The prior order-three shape test flagged 477. The six added cases came from six recordings and were 4.62 percent of the 130 curves that passed the prior test. The largest numerical distance gap over 1125 complete curves was below 0.000000060. Synthetic checks, an independent numerical audit, and an alternate-grid repeat passed. At a ten-trial minimum, no added failure remained at 0.10 in only 37 curves. The error limit is assumed, not measured. Separate trials, protocol drift, nominal timing, shared normalization, slice selection and sparse human data prevent a biological model rejection or a population-rate claim. Code, a proof, aggregate evidence, figures and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External record-level data are excluded.
